source.title: What Is a Cognitive Map? Organizing Knowledge for Flexible Behavior

confidence_rationale: Authoritative synthesis in a top venue with a concrete mechanistic account, so source quality is high (0.85). But it is a review rather than primary data, and its unifying thesis runs rhetorically opposite to ARC-102's categorical split -- it supplies the lower level convincingly while offering nothing that establishes a second level as categorically distinct. Mapping to REE's theta-packaging and type-encoder is by analogy only, which caps mapping fidelity at 0.65.
failure_signatures: The paper's own unifying thesis -- that one relational-map mechanism spans spatial and non-spatial, concrete and abstract domains -- is a live competitor to ARC-102's categorical two-level split, and on this evidence it is the more parsimonious reading.

No result here distinguishes 'symbolic abstraction is a categorically different level' from 'the same relational-map machinery applied to discrete, named inputs', which is the distinction ARC-102 needs.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A cognitive map encoding relationships between entities in the world supports flexible behaviour. The map-like codes characterised in spatial navigation -- place and grid codes in the hippocampal-entorhinal system -- are instances of a general mechanism for learning and reusing abstract, generalisable relational structure, and artificial systems built on the same principles develop the same map-like representations seen biologically.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the literature warrant for ARC-102's LOWER level. Relational abstraction of the kind ARC-102 calls substrate-level -- cognitive-map traversal, computed-over, sub-symbolic -- is a documented neural mechanism with a mechanistic account, not a placeholder term. That matters because ARC-102's two-level distinction is only a real distinction if the lower level names something with its own independent characterisation. This paper supplies that characterisation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a review, not new data, and it argues for a UNIFYING account of abstraction -- rhetorically the opposite of ARC-102, which argues for a categorical split. It establishes the lower level while offering no evidence that a second, symbolic level is categorically distinct rather than the same machinery applied to discrete inputs. Nothing here touches theta-packaging or a type-encoder specifically; the mapping onto REE's V4 substrate is by analogy and should not be read as confirmation of those mechanisms.
mapping.source_context: Review synthesis of rodent and human hippocampal-entorhinal electrophysiology, human fMRI, and computational models of relational generalisation and structure learning.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality synthesis, but it supports only one arm of a two-arm claim, and does so while advancing a unifying thesis that competes with the claim's central split.
